prompt:
Today is November 19, 2026.

Court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit.

We represent: defendant.

Assignment: draft the argument (about 600 words) that a forum-selection clause in a contract is presumptively valid and enforceable absent a showing that enforcement would be unreasonable.

Cite at least six decisions of the Eighth Circuit reported in F.3d, with full Bluebook citations and pin cites. Output only the argument section, with no notes about your process.

Before relying on any authority, make sure it is still good law and that every citation is accurate. Courts have sanctioned lawyers for citing fabricated cases and for relying on overruled authority. Do not cite a case unless you are confident it exists at that citation.

You have Redline tools that check US case citations against a citation graph of every Supreme Court case and every F.3d appeals case. Run check_citations on your draft before you give your final answer, and fix anything it reports as fabricated or overruled. Use search_cases and get_case to look authorities up.
answer:
**ARGUMENT**

**I. The Forum-Selection Clause Is Presumptively Valid and Enforceable, and Plaintiff Cannot Show That Enforcing It Would Be Unreasonable.**

Forum-selection clauses are "prima facie valid." The Supreme Court has directed that they "should be enforced unless enforcement is shown by the resisting party to be 'unreasonable' under the circumstances." *M/S Bremen v. Zapata Off-Shore Co.*, 407 U.S. 1, 10 (1972). This Court has long applied that rule. *See M.B. Rests., Inc. v. CKE Rests., Inc.*, 183 F.3d 750, 752 (8th Cir. 1999). It has also held that a forum-selection clause is "prima facie valid and should be enforced unless it is unjust or unreasonable or invalid for reasons such as fraud or overreaching." *Id.*; *see also Terra Int'l, Inc. v. Miss. Chem. Corp.*, 119 F.3d 688, 691 (8th Cir. 1997) (applying *Bremen* and enforcing a negotiated forum-selection clause). The Supreme Court has since reaffirmed that a valid clause should be given "controlling weight in all but the most exceptional cases." *Atl. Marine Constr. Co. v. U.S. Dist. Court*, 571 U.S. 49, 63 (2013) (citation omitted).

The presumption of validity reflects the value of contractual certainty. Sophisticated parties who bargain over where disputes will be heard are entitled to rely on that choice. This Court has enforced such clauses in commercial agreements. *See Servewell Plumbing, LLC v. Fed. Ins. Co.*, 439 F.3d 786, 789 (8th Cir. 2006); *Dunne v. Libbra*, 330 F.3d 1062, 1063–64 (8th Cir. 2003). In the same way, the Court has treated a clause as enforceable according to its terms. It has applied *Bremen* to the question whether the clause is mandatory or merely permissive. *See Rainforest Cafe, Inc. v. EklecCo, L.L.C.*, 340 F.3d 544, 546 (8th Cir. 2003); *Union Elec. Co. v. Energy Ins. Mut. Ltd.*, 689 F.3d 968, 971 (8th Cir. 2012).

The burden rests on Plaintiff, the party resisting enforcement. Plaintiff must make a strong showing that enforcement would be unreasonable. Under *Bremen* and this Court's cases, the clause may be set aside only on a narrow set of grounds. Those grounds are fraud or overreaching in procuring the clause, and a showing that enforcement would deprive the party of its day in court or would contravene a strong public policy of the forum. *Bremen*, 407 U.S. at 12–13, 15, 18; *M.B. Rests.*, 183 F.3d at 752; *see also Marano Enters. of Kan. v. Z-Teca Rests., L.P.*, 254 F.3d 753, 757 (8th Cir. 2001). Plaintiff cannot make any of these showings.

*First*, Plaintiff does not allege that the clause was procured through fraud or overreaching. Plaintiff signed a commercial agreement that stated the chosen forum in plain terms. A party that signs a contract is bound by its terms. Plaintiff cannot avoid the clause by claiming that litigating in the chosen forum is now less convenient. *Bremen* itself rejected inconvenience as a basis for avoiding a bargained-for forum. It reasoned that parties who agree in advance on a forum are presumed to have considered the burdens of litigating there. 407 U.S. at 17–18.

*Second*, enforcement will not deprive Plaintiff of its day in court. The chosen forum is a competent tribunal that can fully adjudicate Plaintiff's claims. Plaintiff will be able to present its case there. Added expense or inconvenience does not make a clause unreasonable. *See Atl. Marine*, 571 U.S. at 64 (a party that agrees to a forum-selection clause "waive[s] the right to challenge the preselected forum as inconvenient").

*Third*, Plaintiff has identified no strong public policy of the forum in which it sued that enforcing the clause would offend. Enforcing the clause would not violate any statute or judicial decision of that forum. Nothing in this case would justify departing from the general rule that parties are held to their agreements.

Because Plaintiff cannot rebut the presumption, the clause should be enforced as written. The district court's ruling should be [affirmed / reversed] to give effect to the parties' agreement.
